title: Notion vs Obsidian for Teams 2026: Knowledge Base Showdown
description: Notion vs Obsidian for team knowledge bases compared: collaboration features, pricing at scale, setup complexity, and which tool actually gets used by your team.

features.name: Collaboration
features.tool2Detail: Obsidian uses file sync, no real-time collab

features.name: Pricing (10 users)
features.tool2Detail: Obsidian is free for personal use, 50 dollars/user/yr for Sync

features.name: Setup Time
features.tool2Detail: Obsidian requires building your own system

features.name: Offline Access
features.tool1Detail: Notion requires internet for most features
features.tool2Detail: Obsidian stores files locally, works offline

features.name: Data Ownership
features.tool1Detail: Notion data lives on their servers
features.tool2Detail: Obsidian stores everything as local Markdown files

verdict: For teams, Notion wins. Real-time collaboration, easier onboarding, and built-in templates make it the practical choice for most organizations. Obsidian is better for technical teams who prefer Markdown, need offline access, or want data stored locally. Start with Notion. Only consider Obsidian if your team is technically proficient and values data ownership.

faqs.question: Can Obsidian be used as a team knowledge base?
faqs.answer: Yes, with limitations. Obsidian supports team collaboration through Obsidian Sync at 50 dollars/user/year and published sites. However, it lacks real-time co-editing, has a steeper learning curve, and requires technical proficiency with Markdown.

faqs.question: How much does Notion cost for a 10-person team?
faqs.answer: Notion Plus costs 80 dollars/month for 10 users at 8 dollars/user/mo. The free tier supports unlimited members but lacks some collaboration features. For most teams, Plus is the recommended plan.

faqs.question: Which is better for developers?
faqs.answer: Obsidian is better for developers. It stores files as local Markdown, supports Git version control, and has a powerful plugin ecosystem. Developers appreciate the plain-text approach and command-line integration.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Obsidian to Notion?
faqs.answer: Yes, migration takes 1-2 weeks. Export Obsidian vault as Markdown files, then import to Notion using the Markdown import feature. Some formatting and links may need manual cleanup. Plan for 20-30 hours of work for a large knowledge base.

faqs.question: Which tool is better for a 50-person team?
faqs.answer: Notion is better for teams over 20 people. Real-time collaboration, admin controls, and SSO make it more manageable at scale. Obsidian sync costs and lack of admin features make it impractical for large teams.
